testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Water on a roadway can cause:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hydroplaning.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water collects on the road surface.

questions.question: If you notice a safety or mechanical problem with your vehicle while driving, you should:

options.text: Stay quiet and see if the problem goes away.
Write down your concerns in a report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write down your concerns in a report.
questions.explanation: At the end of each day, you must write a report about any vehicle problems. Note any issues that could affect safety or cause a mechanical breakdown.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Watch gauges for signs of trouble.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch gauges for signs of trouble.
questions.explanation: Watch your vehicle's gauges while driving for signs of trouble. Check gauges before starting a trip to make sure they work properly.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will need to:

options.text: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
Guess the weight of cargo on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your entire vehicle. Explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle set by the manufacturer
The maximum weight a vehicle can tow
The minimum weight a vehicle can carry

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle set by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: The GVWR is the maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle that the manufacturer specifies.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems has water and oil in it. This can damage the system if it builds up. Air tanks have drain valves to remove water and oil.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while driving downhill and there is no escape ramp, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive into an open field.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a hill, look for an escape ramp first. If none is available, find another place to stop, like an open field or a side road that goes uphill or flattens out.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of bad brakes?

options.text: Pads that are clean and dry

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads that are clean and dry
questions.explanation: Check for cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil or grease, and shoes that are worn thin, broken, or missing. Clean, dry pads are normal.

questions.question: If you must drive in reverse, backing toward the driver's side:

options.text: Is only recommended if it is raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is always encouraged.
questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side when you must reverse. As the driver, you will have the best view of where you are going.

questions.question: After an accident, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Move your vehicle to the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive away from the scene
questions.explanation: After an accident, protect the area, call police, help the injured, collect information, and report the accident. Leaving the scene can cost you your license.

questions.question: Vehicles driving behind a truck:

options.text: May have difficulty seeing objects in front of the truck.
Often have a great view of the roadway in front of them.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have difficulty seeing objects in front of the truck.
questions.explanation: A truck blocks the view of drivers behind it. They may not see hazards ahead. Flash your brakes to warn other drivers when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What is a retarder?

options.text: A device that prevents a vehicle from going too fast
A device that prevents a vehicle from being too loud
A device that improves a vehicle's gas mileage

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that prevents a vehicle from going too fast
questions.explanation: A retarder slows down a vehicle. It reduces how much drivers need to use the brakes.

questions.question: If backing a truck:

options.text: You should rely on your mirrors to guide you.
You should first walk the area to check for obstacles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should first walk the area to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk around your vehicle to look at the path and check for obstacles. Mirrors have blind spots, so you cannot rely on them alone. Use a helper when possible.

questions.question: While driving, if you notice an unusual noise or feeling, you should:

options.text: Assume it is not a concern and keep driving.
Hope the vehicle makes it until another driver takes over.
Stop and check to find the problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check to find the problem.
questions.explanation: Use your senses while driving to spot mechanical problems. If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual, stop and check it out.

questions.question: After driving a short distance following a tire change, you should stop to:

options.text: Make sure the lug nuts are still tight.
Make sure the tire is wearing evenly.
Make sure the tire air pressure is acceptable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the lug nuts are still tight.
questions.explanation: After driving a short distance following a tire change, stop to recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections should be done:

options.text: Differently each time to focus on different items.
The same way each time so you do not forget anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you do not forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way before every drive. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you check everything.

questions.question: When driving in hot weather:

options.text: Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.
questions.explanation: Heat increases tire air pressure, so check tire pressure in hot weather. To prevent engine overheating, keep enough oil in the engine and enough water and antifreeze in the cooling system. Antifreeze helps in both hot and cold weather.

questions.question: When driving in winter, what needs extra attention in a pre-trip inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Coolant and antifreeze levels
questions.explanation: In winter, pay special attention to coolant and antifreeze levels, defroster and heater, wiper blades and washer fluid, tires and chains, lights and reflectors, windows and mirrors, steps and handholds, radiator shutters, winterfront, and exhaust system.

questions.question: A danger of swerving to avoid a hazard in a large truck is:

options.text: The truck may miss the object.
The truck may stay in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck may flip over.
questions.explanation: Swerving can sometimes be the safest choice, but it has risks. Top-heavy vehicles and tractors with multiple trailers may flip over when swerving.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
The weight of the tire itself

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum safe weight that a tire can carry at a specified pressure.

questions.question: If brakes fail on a long downgrade, what should the driver do?

options.text: Turn the vehicle off and then back on to reset the brakes.
Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, use an escape ramp if available. If not, look for another escape route, such as a side road or open field.

questions.question: How should you hold a steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand while the other hand rests.
With both hands to ensure a firm grip.
Release it if the vehicle is approaching a bump.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands to ensure a firm grip.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of when to change gears?

options.text: The speed of the vehicle next to you

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of the vehicle next to you
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift gears. First is engine speed (rpm)—read your vehicle's manual to learn when to shift up. Second is road speed (mph)—learn which speeds work for each gear, then watch your speedometer and shift as needed.

questions.question: What do the two systems of a dual air brake system share?
questions.correctAnswerText: An air compressor
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the compressor fails, neither system will work.

questions.question: What happens if a tire has too much air pressure?

options.text: It is good for long drives.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Never put too much air pressure in a tire. Check your tire pressure with a gauge during inspections.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, why should you turn toward the driver's side?

options.text: Because it gives the driver a better view.
Because turning toward the passenger side is illegal.
Because other drivers can offer assistance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because it gives the driver a better view.
questions.explanation: When backing up, back toward the driver's side. This gives you the best view of your path.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and blocking other drivers, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to alert drivers behind you (if local laws allow).

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, what should the driver do?

options.text: Pull out the air brake knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal down.
questions.explanation: To make a normal stop in a vehicle with air brakes, press the brake pedal down.

questions.question: What should your horn be used for?

options.text: To tell other drivers that you are angry.
To warn other drivers that you are near.

questions.correctAnswerText: To warn other drivers that you are near.
questions.explanation: Your horn warns others of your presence. Use it only when necessary, since it can startle other drivers.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: Your view of the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your view of the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be able to stop within the distance you can see ahead. Slow down whenever visibility is reduced.

questions.question: When loading cargo, it is important to:

options.text: Stack items as high as possible.
Know the weight capacity of the suspension system.
Place light items underneath heavier items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know the weight capacity of the suspension system.
questions.explanation: Drivers must make sure their vehicle is not overloaded. They must know the legal weight limits and the maximum weight their vehicle can carry, including the suspension system's weight capacity.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should ensure that the ____ come on automatically when air pressure falls below 45 psi.
questions.correctAnswerText: Spring brakes
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that spring brakes come on automatically when air tank pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. To test this, chock the wheels and release air from the brake system by pressing and releasing the brake pedal. When pressure drops to an unsafe level, the parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should engage.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.correctAnswerText: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997, and other air brake vehicles made on or after March 1, 1998, must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: If driving through flowing water or a large puddle, you should:

options.text: Try to stop in the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: Avoid driving through large puddles or moving water when possible. If you must drive through water, slow down, shift to a low gear, and gently apply the brakes. Pressing the brake linings against the drums or discs keeps water, mud, silt, and sand out of the brake system.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard:

options.text: You should always steer to the left.
You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
You should steer sharply in one direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: In some emergencies, driving onto the shoulder may be the best way to avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support the weight of a large vehicle.

questions.question: When stopping in an emergency situation, you should:

options.text: Veer your trailer to the right and stop.
Veer your trailer to the left and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop in a straight line.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking. Brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight, but still allows you to turn if needed.

questions.question: Loading cargo improperly:
questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Proper cargo loading and securing is essential for safety. Improperly loaded cargo can damage your vehicle or cause injury or death if it falls off during a collision or sudden stop.

questions.question: A cracked rim should be:

options.text: Relocated to one of a pair of dual tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Replaced.
questions.explanation: Inspect wheels before driving for damage. Do not use wheels or rims that have been welded. They are not safe.

questions.question: Texting while driving is especially dangerous because:

options.text: It is both a mental and physical distraction.
A message may be upsetting to the driver.
People like to read and may become too engaged in their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is both a mental and physical distraction.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it distracts your mind and requires you to take at least one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: Cargo being transported should be checked:

options.text: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles of the trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles of the trip.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. Also check it every time you stop to rest. As the driver, you are responsible for keeping the cargo safely secured throughout the entire trip.

questions.question: What do ABS brakes do?

options.text: Stop your wheels from locking up.
Stop your vehicle from speeding up when going uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: A smaller vehicle than yours will usually:

options.text: Take longer to stop than your vehicle.
Take the same time to stop as your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop faster than your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles can stop faster than larger vehicles. Remember this when deciding how far to stay behind another car.

questions.question: On icy roads, a retarder should be:

options.text: Used only on the rear wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turned off.
questions.explanation: A retarder can cause your vehicle to skid on icy roads. Turn it off when traction is poor.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must do all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Get a CIA intelligence check.
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass the HazMat test, complete a federal security check, prove U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, and get an FBI fingerprint check and federal criminal background check.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, belts should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Checked for tightness.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check all belts to make sure they are tight and not worn.

questions.question: When starting the engine during a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Put the engine in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for unusual noises.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine during a pre-trip inspection, listen carefully for any unusual noises.

questions.question: If there is a cargo fire in a box trailer, the doors should:

options.text: Have a heavy blanket placed over them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not be opened.
questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors if there is a cargo fire. Opening the doors gives the fire more oxygen and makes it bigger.

questions.question: Who is responsible for making sure cargo is loaded properly?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for checking the cargo, watching for overloads, making sure cargo is secured properly, and keeping cargo away from emergency equipment.

questions.question: When making a turn during your driving test, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal only if other cars are nearby.
Check traffic only in the direction you are turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: When making a turn during a driving test, always check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: Loading cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Makes your vehicle more likely to tip over.
Makes items more likely to fall down.
Makes the cargo harder to unload.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes your vehicle more likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity increases the risk that your vehicle will roll over. Load cargo to keep the weight balanced and low.
